sealed.statement: After the existing owner has durably completed a priority ADD, entity-scoped priority-recovery observation cannot downgrade that operation to an older CREATING row; it preserves terminal authority or explicitly defers, allowing the existing surplus REMOVE and fresh-formation ready-lease paths to converge.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Before changing production code, reproduce the exact terminal-ADD downgrade through the real ReplicaOperationRepository and control-plane gateway authority contract: confirm the terminal transition, make the later owner-RPC path unavailable while an older SQL CREATING row is visible, and show the entity observation re-admits CREATING on current HEAD. The fixed discriminator must preserve terminal state or return a typed deferred observation, and it must be proven red on revert.

Reuse the existing owner-RPC authority modes, owner-persisted transition witness, terminal-transition repair, complete_priority_recovery_drain action, priority planner, and surplus-remove safety path. Do not add an operation owner, cache, watermark store, timer, retry loop, readiness path, or formation path.

Once the owning persistence path has confirmed a terminal operation version, a later entity-scoped observation used for recovery planning must not expose an older nonterminal version as authoritative. Owner unavailability, empty reads, conflicting identity, or uncertain authority must defer fail-closed rather than infer terminality, absence, or safe removal.

Preserve the current priority ADD completion semantics and existing surplus REMOVE safety checks. The correction must only prevent a stale nonterminal re-entry; it must not force completion, synthesize a REMOVE, bypass voter-ready membership safety, or treat physical replica ACTIVE as durable workflow completion.

Fresh formation must remain fail-closed on genuinely nonterminal operations and unsafe placement, while the landed durable-rejoin cold-formation exemption remains unchanged. Unknown authority must not release the ready lease, and shutdown/cache-only diagnostics must not reopen remote reads.

Do not widen the 120-second formation or restart budgets, lower workload, weaken canonical membership or ready-lease checks, alter statistical bars, or add planner wakeups to mask the repeated CREATING observation.

Run the existing architecture contract model gate, then extend or add the smallest TLA+ model only if the deterministic discriminator proves a temporal authority/observation transition gap not represented by an adjacent model. Alloy is not required unless the correction changes ownership or membership cardinality rather than temporal read authority.

After deterministic, adjacent, model, and independent verification closure on one exact clean commit, run at most one unchanged N=1 rolling-restart diagnostic. Do not spend another N=15 certification window in this child Quest; return any later blocker with exact mechanism evidence to the parent.

The deterministic test was PRESENT with one CREATING operation before the correction and is typed DEFERRED with zero operations after it.
rulesOut: Rules out terminal mutation failure, missing terminal repair, a new planner wake, physical-replica completion inference, and timing changes; the missing contract is monotonic authority at the existing entity observation boundary.

claim: TLC proves the temporal correction and its forbidden shape: the fixed owner-required/deferred route preserves ConfirmedTerminalNeverReentersCreating and eventually reuses the existing surplus REMOVE to reach formation ready, while the stale-SQL fallback mutant violates the terminal monotonicity invariant.
rulesOut: Alloy was not extended because owner and cohort cardinality do not change; the existing core Alloy gate still passes, while TLA+ directly covers the ordering and liveness obligation.
